blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings rose from 63 in June to 66 in October (+4.8%), and it took 3.2% of the city’s 464 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings rose from 79 in June to 84 in October (+6.3%), and it took 6.0% of the city’s 737 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Queen Mary Park for detached houses in July, October (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in August, October (a buyers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Lots and land in Queen Mary Park
What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default form: the feed's stock is detached houses (including large newer custom builds and older basement-entry homes), half duplexes — the feed's first two cards are a half-duplex pair — low-rise condos, townhomes, and at least one manufactured-home park address on 134 Street (park facts are not confirmed). Detached stock is predominantly freehold; a sub-area tenure split is not published on an official source: not confirmed.

Bare-land strata — the form, no Queen Mary Park instance verified: A bare-land strata lot is strata tenure ON the lot itself: the buyer takes a strata lot, pays strata fees, is bound by the strata's bylaws, and is entitled to a Form B Information Certificate for the lot — it is not fee-simple ownership. Tenure is read lot by lot on title.

Lot character: detached lots in the first-page listings run from roughly 5,000 sq ft half-duplex lots to roughly 9,000 sq ft custom-build lots, with lane and cul-de-sac pockets. That is an observation from listings, not a zoning statement, and no area-wide lot-size table is published. Any specific lot's zone (Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000, shown in the City's COSMOS map), area and subdivision minimum are a parcel check and are not confirmed per lot here.

Suite / multi-unit character of the ground: Suite and multi-unit use is a visible part of the detached profile: first-page detached listings describe basement suites, side suites and multi-suite half duplexes marketed for multi-generational living and rental income.
ALR vs non-ALR split

Assemblies / proposals — documented as such, never as inventory: King George Boulevard BRT (approximately 19 km, 12 stations, now in full design) running along the sub-area's eastern edge is a corridor plan fact, not lots for sale.

Manufactured-home park address — documented as a feed fact only: The feed includes a manufactured-home park address on 134 Street (the same address appears in the surrey-mobile-homes feed); park facts (age restriction, pad rent, rules) are not verified here — no park-operator source was opened, and listing text was deliberately not used. A pad-rental home is not a fee-simple lot purchase.

items.t: Municipality and community: City of Surrey; the sub-area sits at the meeting of the City-published Whalley / City Centre side (north) and Newton side (south) of central Surrey. Which City community each address falls in is address-specific: Not verified as an area-wide statement.
Nearby: Bear Creek Park, 13750 88 Ave, at the sub-area's northeast, and Queen Elizabeth Meadows Park, 9400 134 St.

Nearby and related areas: Bear Creek Green Timbers (east, across King George Boulevard), Cedar Hills and West Newton (south), Whalley (north), and Scottsdale / North Delta across Scott Road to the west.
Parent Surrey medians (sub-area medians are not published): detached $1,215,000; attached $512,944. No detached figure is a land figure.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Queen Mary Park

items.t: BC strata block (wherever a strata lot — including a bare-land strata lot — is the purchase): Form B within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25¢/page; depreciation reports every 5 years for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions). A "45+" listing line is not a valid age bylaw.

ALR block — conditional, no ALR ground documented for this sub-area: If a parcel were in the ALR: residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha); farm class in FULL three-tier form ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha / $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha / $10,000 under 0.8 ha, applications by October 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

blocks.text: Good to know about Queen Mary Park

items.t: Detached barely moved here in September 2026 while attached carried the sub-area.

Two RapidBus corridors bracket the sub-area, and a third transit plan is in design. The R1 (King George Blvd) and R6 (Scott Road) RapidBus corridors run on its east and west edges today; King George Boulevard BRT (approximately 19 km, 12 stations) is in full design along the eastern edge — current service versus plan, stated separately.
No catchment from another Surrey area transfers here.

blocks.text: Mobile and manufactured homes in Queen Mary Park
Verified park inside Queen Mary Park: 1 — Westwood Estates, pad rental.
The parks and communities

items.t: Westwood Estates: Plainly: a home here sits on a rented pad — the buyer owns the home (a chattel) and rents the pad; the buyer does not own the land. The tenancy is governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, not the Strata Property Act.

Address note: current listings use both 8224 134 Street and 8254 134 Street as the park address (different postal codes appear with each: V3W 4V1 with 8224, V3W 6M2 with 8254) — confirm the civic address and pad number from the park office before a showing or an offer. A fresh search check on Nov 2, 2026 returned current listings under both addresses, each naming Westwood Estates, Queen Mary Park Surrey, and "Senior Community: Yes" in the MLS data — the conflict is live, not historical.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Queen Mary Park

items.t: "Queen Mary Park" is a Fraser Valley board sub-area in central Surrey, west of King George Boulevard and south of 96 Avenue, taking its name from Queen Mary Park, the City park at 8972 Queen Mary Blvd, Surrey. Formal boundaries: Not verified — no City of Surrey neighbourhood or plan-area boundary for "Queen Mary Park" as a residential area was confirmed on an official source; the name is a board sub-area name and a City park name, and page copy should present it as such, not as a City planning district.
Nearby: Bear Creek Park, 13750 88 Ave, at the sub-area's northeast.

Where the mobile-home stock sits: the one verified park, Westwood Estates, is on 134 Street at the sub-area's southeast edge, just south of 88 Avenue and a short walk from Bear Creek Park in its listings' description.

blocks.text: Good to know about Queen Mary Park

items.t: This park's own listings cannot agree on its address or its pad rent: A fresh Nov 2, 2026 search check returned the same two addresses and the same rent spread on current listings.
Two Surrey parks share almost the same name, in two different sub-areas: An alert set on one name does not cover the other park, and a showing booked off the wrong park is a wasted trip.

blocks.text: Queen Mary Park Surrey: streets and boundaries

items.t: Queen Mary Park is a Fraser Valley board sub-area in central Surrey, west of King George Boulevard and south of 96 Avenue, named for the City park at its centre — it is a board and local name, not a City of Surrey plan area.

The City's own park page places Queen Mary Park north of 88 Avenue and west of 132 Street, and the City places the park under its "Whalley and City Centre" community grouping even though the surrounding blocks sit at the meeting of the Whalley side (north) and the Newton side (south) of central Surrey.
Bear Creek Green Timbers is east across King George Boulevard, Cedar Hills and West Newton are south, Whalley is north, and Scottsdale / North Delta lie across Scott Road (120 Street) to the west.
No City neighbourhood or plan-area boundary for a "Queen Mary Park" residential district was confirmed on an official source: do not treat any street line quoted elsewhere as a City boundary.

blocks.text: Queen Mary Park Surrey: the housing stock

items.t: The stock is detached houses — older basement-entry homes, half duplexes and newer custom builds — with low-rise condos and townhomes at the edges and at least one manufactured-home park address on 134 Street.

Suite use is a defining feature of the detached stock here: houses are commonly described with basement suites, side suites and multi-suite half duplexes used for multi-generational living and rental income, which is why suite legality matters more in this sub-area than in most of Surrey.
Queen Elizabeth Meadows Park, 9400 134 St, anchors the sub-area's east edge, across from a townhome complex on 134 Street.

blocks.text: Queen Mary Park Surrey: rules that affect buyers

items.t: One secondary suite is the Surrey limit: the City permits only one suite per single-family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling unit, at most 40% of the principal unit's habitable floor area, and never inside a coach house or garden suite — a multi-suite listing here needs a legality check, not just a rent estimate.

Healy Creek runs through Queen Mary Park and the park's natural areas exist to protect its ecosystem, so lots backing onto the park or the creek can carry riparian setback and tree rules — check the parcel in the City's COSMOS map.

blocks.text: Queen Mary Park Surrey: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Queen Mary Park's trails start at two unmarked-feeling points: the intersection of Queen Mary Boulevard and 130B Street, and the end of Lanark Place east of Queen Mary Boulevard, with the playground reached from the trails in the middle of the park.

The park is mostly protected natural area, not sports fields: the City states the majority of the park is natural areas established to protect the sensitive ecosystem of Healy Creek, an important tributary to Bear Creek and the Serpentine River.
The two secondary schools beside the sub-area are Queen Elizabeth Secondary (9457 King George Blvd) and L.A.
Route 321 runs the length of King George Boulevard past the sub-area's east edge, from Surrey Central Station via Newton Exchange to White Rock Centre — the one-seat bus ride to White Rock.
The nearest full grocery anchor is at Central City, 10153 King George Blvd in City Centre, where T&T Supermarket anchors the mall.

Measured from the park (8972 Queen Mary Boulevard) in the What's Nearby pass: King George Station is a 4.7-minute drive (3.00 km) and Surrey Central Station a 6.4-minute drive (3.93 km), OSRM routing measured 2026-11-02.

blocks.text: Queen Mary Park Surrey: development and new projects

items.t: King George Boulevard Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) (City of Surrey / TransLink) — approximately 19 kilometres and 12 stations from Surrey City Centre to Semiahmoo Town Centre, running along this sub-area's eastern edge on King George Boulevard; status: Council has approved the next design stage (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Queen Mary Park Surrey: getting around

items.t: The R1 King George Blvd RapidBus runs on the sub-area's east edge and the R6 Scott Road RapidBus on its west edge — two rapid corridors, one on each side, both feeding Expo Line stations.
Route 324 runs via 132 Street between Surrey Central Station and Newton Exchange, crossing the sub-area's east side north–south.
Route 321 runs on King George Boulevard from Surrey Central Station via Newton Exchange to White Rock Centre.
The nearest SkyTrain station is King George Station, the Expo Line terminus in City Centre, north of the sub-area.

blocks.text: Queen Mary Park Surrey: risks and due diligence

items.t: Healy Creek is the local constraint layer: the creek is a tributary to Bear Creek and the Serpentine River and its ecosystem is the reason most of Queen Mary Park is protected natural area, so any lot draining to or backing onto the creek corridor should be checked for riparian setbacks in COSMOS.

Surrey's mapped floodplain lowlands — the Nicomekl and Serpentine coastal floodplain and the Little Campbell River area — are south of this upland sub-area, but the Serpentine system is the same watershed Healy Creek feeds, so a low lot near the creek is a parcel-level check, not a neighbourhood assumption.

Suite legality is the financial due-diligence item here: an unauthorized suite can fail financing and insurance checks, and the City's suite page — one suite per unit, 40% maximum — is the standard to test the property against.

faq.q: Is Queen Mary Park an official City neighbourhood with set boundaries?
faq.a: No boundary was confirmed: the name is a City park name and a Fraser Valley board sub-area name, with no City plan area by this name. The feed span (Scott Road to 134 Street, 81 Avenue to 96 Avenue) is a listing observation, not a boundary.

faq.q: Is there a vacant lot I can buy here?
faq.a: No bare-land subdivision is verified — the purchase is an existing fee-simple house lot (detached or half-duplex stock) for rebuild, added units or suite use.

faq.q: Can a detached lot here add units?
faq.a: Under Surrey's SSMUH framework, most eligible lots under 4,050 m² inside the Urban Containment Boundary can carry 3 units (under 280 m²) or 4 units (280 m² or more), and eligible lots within 400 m of a frequent bus stop can carry up to 6 — check the parcel's zone and Frequent Bus Stop Area status in COSMOS.

faq.q: Are basement suites allowed in these houses?
faq.a: Surrey permits one secondary suite per single-family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling unit, at most 40% of the principal unit's habitable floor area, never inside a coach house or garden suite. A specific home's suite legality must be confirmed with the City — listings in this sub-area include homes described with unauthorized suites.

faq.q: Which schools serve a lot here — is it Queen Mary Park Elementary?
faq.a: There is no school by that name — the name comes from the City park. The Ministry-listed elementaries for this ground are David Brankin, Senator Reid, Betty Huff, Kennedy Trail and Kirkbride, with Queen Elizabeth and L.A. Run the exact address in the SD36 School Locator.

faq.q: At Westwood Estates, do I own the land?
faq.a: No. You own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — the park owns the land, and your right to the site is the assigned pad tenancy under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act. Plainly, a home on a rented pad is not land ownership.

faq.q: What is the park's address — 8224 or 8254 134 Street?
faq.a: Both appear on current listings for the same park, with different postal codes — an open conflict, confirmed live again on a Nov 2, 2026 search check. Confirm the civic address and pad number from the park office; do not navigate or write an offer off a listing's address alone.

A park's age rule lives in its park rules and tenancy documents, not in a strata bylaw, so the written park rules are the deciding document; the MHPTA assignment rules recognise a 55+ park (at least one tenant on the site 55 or older) and let the owner refuse an assignment where no purchaser meets the requirement. Get the park's current rule in writing.

faq.q: My spouse is under 55 — can we both live there?
faq.a: In a strata, provincial rules exempt a younger spouse or partner. In Westwood Estates, the park's own rules govern who may reside — the strata exemptions do not automatically apply to a pad tenancy, so ask the park for its rule in writing before writing.

faq.q: Is there a Queen Mary Park Elementary School?
faq.a: No school by that name exists in Surrey. The British Columbia Ministry K-12 list for School District 36 has no Queen Mary Park Elementary — the Queen Mary elementaries in the provincial list are in Vancouver and North Vancouver. This sub-area is named for the City park, not a school, and its elementaries are David Brankin, Senator Reid, Betty Huff, Kennedy Trail and Kirkbride.

faq.q: Which elementary school will my child attend?
faq.a: Schools confirmed by address in or beside the sub-area are David Brankin Elementary (9160 128 St), Senator Reid Elementary (9341 126 St), Betty Huff Elementary (13055 Huntley Ave), Kennedy Trail Elementary (8305 122a St) and Kirkbride Elementary (12150 92 Ave). Run the address in the SD36 School Locator before relying on one.

faq.q: Are the basement suites in these houses legal?
faq.a: Not always — verify each one with the City. Surrey permits one secondary suite per dwelling unit at most 40% of the principal unit's habitable floor area, and homes in this sub-area are openly described in listings as having unauthorized suites. A suite's permit status affects financing, insurance and whether the rental income can be counted at all.

faq.q: How do I get downtown without a car?
faq.a: Two RapidBus corridors frame the sub-area: the R1 King George Blvd runs on King George Boulevard at the east side and the R6 Scott Road runs on Scott Road (120 Street) at the west side, both connecting to Expo Line stations. Local route 324 also runs via 132 Street between Surrey Central Station and Newton Exchange.
